title: Exodus 8 & 9

bullets.text: God heard His people crying out in Egypt and chose Moses to speak to Pharaoh, the mighty king.
Pharaoh kept saying **NO!** — so God sent more and more plagues.

prompt: Today we meet three more amazing plagues!

title: Last Week's Lesson
prompt: God kept His people safe through every single one!

bullets.text: How did God **keep His people safe** each time?
Why is saying **yes** to God but not doing it still saying **no?**

title:
"You have turned against God.
That is worse than using magic."
"Dear God, thank you for this amazing story about how great and mighty you are! Help us learn and trust you just like Moses did. Amen!"
footer: Close your eyes and say it with me... 👇

title: God Sends Moses

body.text: Early one morning, God sent Moses to stand by the river. When Pharaoh walked past, Moses gave him God's message:
"Let my people go! If you don't — flies will fill your whole land!"

prompt: What do you think Pharaoh said? 🤔

title: Flies Everywhere!

body.text: Swarms and swarms of flies filled all of Egypt — in the houses, in the food, in the fields. **Everywhere!**
It was a big, buzzy, horrible mess!

prompt: Can you buzz like a fly? 🪰🪰🪰

title: God Protects His People

body.text: But where God's people lived — in the land of Goshen — there were **NO flies.** Not a single one!
God kept His people completely safe and separate.

prompt: God always knows where YOU are too! 💛

title: Pharaoh's Empty Promise

body.text: Pharaoh said: "Pray to God to take the flies away, and you may go!" Moses prayed, and every fly disappeared.
But then Pharaoh changed his mind **again** and would not keep his promise.

prompt: Saying yes to God but not doing it is still saying no.

title: Another Warning

body.text: God sent Moses to Pharaoh again: "Let my people go! If you refuse, tomorrow all the animals in Egypt will become very, very sick."
God gave Pharaoh a warning and a chance to listen.

prompt: God always gives us a chance to do the right thing!

body.text: The very next day, all the horses, donkeys, camels, cows and sheep of the Egyptians became very sick.
Pharaoh had been warned — but he would **not** listen to God.

title: But God's People...

body.text: Pharaoh sent servants to check the Israelites' animals. Not a single one was sick — every one was perfectly healthy!
God kept His people's animals safe, **exactly** as He promised.

prompt: When God makes a promise, He always keeps it! ✅

title: Moses Throws Ashes

body.text: God told Moses to grab big handfuls of dark ashes and throw them up into the sky, right in front of Pharaoh!
Up, up, up the ashes floated over all of Egypt.

prompt: Raise your hands and pretend to throw ashes! 👐

title: Ouch! Boils Everywhere!

body.text: As the ashes floated down, sore bumps called **boils** broke out on every person and animal in Egypt.
Even Pharaoh's magicians had boils so bad they couldn't stand up!

prompt: Have you ever had an ouchie? This was worse! 😟

title: Pharaoh Still Said No

body.text: Even with boils all around him, Pharaoh's heart was still hard. He still would not let God's people go.
The more he refused God, the harder his heart became.

prompt: Obey God fully — and obey today!

title: Angela's Diary
footer: Today I'm writing about... Sneaky Pharaoh!

title: Sneaky Trick #1 🪤

body.text: Teacher showed us SNEAKY PHARAOH today! First he said, "Okay — but only sacrifice right here in Egypt!" He didn't really want to obey; he just wanted it his own way.
Pharaoh tried to avoid obeying by making Israel sacrifice in Egypt.

teacher_note: Exodus 8:25–27 — Pharaoh said worship God INSIDE Egypt. The animals Israel would sacrifice were sacred to the Egyptians, so doing it openly could have gotten them stoned (8:26). Obedience on Pharaoh's terms — a possible trap.

title: Sneaky Trick #2 ⏰

body.text: Then Moses said, "I will pray to the Lord, and TOMORROW the flies will leave." But why wait? Teacher says if he was repentant, he would have begged that the flies disappear immediately — not later.
This is delayed obedience.

teacher_note: Exodus 8:9–10 — Pharaoh chose "tomorrow" for relief when he could have asked for it at once. A repentant heart would have begged for immediate deliverance; delay was his way of holding on to control.

title: Sneaky Trick #3 🤥

body.text: Every time Pharaoh promised "Yes, you can go!" he was telling a LIE. Moses told him to stop. Telling lies is what the devil does — and Pharaoh was copying him.
Pharaoh was a liar, like his master, the devil.

teacher_note: Exodus 8:28–29 (cf. John 8:44) — Moses says it plainly: "let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more." Lying is the devil's nature; Pharaoh mirrors his master.

title: Sneaky Trick #4 ⚖️

body.text: God drew a LINE! On His people's side — bright, safe Goshen — no flies and no sick animals. On Pharaoh's side — plague after plague. Obeying only halfway keeps you on the wrong side of the line.
Partial obedience has painful rewards.

teacher_note: Exodus 8:22–23; 9:4–6 — God set Goshen apart, sparing His people. Obeying God only partway leaves us on the wrong side of the line, reaping consequences plague after plague. Full obedience is the only safe place.

body.text: "Dear God, you are so powerful and SO good. Help me to obey you ALL the way — not halfway like Sneaky Pharaoh."
"Thank you for keeping me safe too. I love you, God! Amen."

title: Three More Plagues

bullets.text: **Plague 4:** Flies filled Egypt — but not Goshen!
**Plague 5:** Egypt's animals got sick — Israel's were fine!
**Plague 6:** Boils on all Egypt — but God's people were safe!

prompt: Obey God fully — not halfway like Pharaoh! ❤️
